classification.difficultyReason: Build unsupplied intermediate relationships using equal radii, central and circumference angles, and intersecting lines. The hardest parts require envisaging an auxiliary radius, combining central sectors and returning to an isosceles triangle to obtain OAB.

spec.description: Circle, triangle ABC, radii OA and OB, centre marker and external 32° pointer at C.
spec.mathematics: The angle ACB is 32° and O is the centre.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB &= 2\times32^\circ\\&=64^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $OA=OB$, triangle $AOB$ is isosceles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle OAB &= \frac{180^\circ-64^\circ}{2}\\&=58^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle ABC and radii OA, OB and OC; separate external pointers identify the two angles at C.
spec.mathematics: Angle ACO is 12° and angle OCB is 25°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two given angles are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB &=12^\circ+25^\circ\\&=37^\circ\\\angle AOB &=2\times37^\circ\\&=74^\circ\end{align*}$$
The centre angle is twice the circumference angle on the same arc. Since $OA=OB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OAB &=\frac{180^\circ-74^\circ}{2}\\&=53^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with an unlabelled upper-right vertex, radii OB and OA, and external 18° and 21° pointers.
spec.mathematics: The given angles are between OB and the upper chord at B, and between OA and the upper chord at A.
spec.answerVisibility: The upper-right point has no printed label; no answer is shown.

answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the unlabelled point. Since $OB=OP$ and $OA=OP$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BPO &=18^\circ\\\angle OPA &=21^\circ\\\angle BPA &=18^\circ+21^\circ\\&=39^\circ\\\angle BOA &=2\times39^\circ\\&=78^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $OA=OB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OAB &=\frac{180^\circ-78^\circ}{2}\\&=51^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with unlabelled bottom vertex, radii OA and OB, 19° at A and 26° at B.
spec.mathematics: The 19° and 26° givens lie between each radius and the chord to the bottom point.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied angles are shown.

answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the unlabelled bottom point. Since $OA=OP$ and $OB=OP$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle APO &=19^\circ\\\angle OPB &=26^\circ\\\angle APB &=19^\circ+26^\circ\\&=45^\circ\\\angle AOB &=2\times45^\circ\\&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $OA=OB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OAB &=\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}\\&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Chord AB crosses the radius to the unlabelled lower-right point. The source 48° pointer identifies the angle at B between its two chords; the 65° pointer identifies the acute crossing sector.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABD is 48°. The acute crossing angle BXD is 65°, vertically opposite AXO. D and X are internal code names only.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither unlabelled point receives a printed name. The supplied answer 19° is omitted.

answer.worked:
Let $D$ be the unlabelled circumference point and $X$ the crossing. The centre angle is twice the circumference angle on arc $AD$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOD &=2\times48^\circ\\&=96^\circ\end{align*}$$
Vertically opposite angles give $\angle AXO=65^\circ$. Since $X$ lies on $OD$ and $AB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OAB &=180^\circ-96^\circ-65^\circ\\&=19^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two chords from B, radii to A and the unlabelled upper-left point, and external 57° and 36° pointers.
spec.mathematics: The angle between the upper-left radius and its chord to B is 57°; the angle between the two chords at B is 36°.
spec.answerVisibility: The upper-left point remains unlabelled; only givens are shown.

answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the unlabelled upper-left point. Since $OP=OB$, $\angle PBO=57^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle POB &=180^\circ-2\times57^\circ\\&=66^\circ\\\angle POA &=2\times36^\circ\\&=72^\circ\\\angle BOA &=66^\circ+72^\circ\\&=138^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angle $POA$ is twice the circumference angle $PBA$. Since $OA=OB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OAB &=\frac{180^\circ-138^\circ}{2}\\&=21^\circ\end{align*}$$
